title: A finite algebra is split reduced or has a dual-number quotient
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $A$ be a commutative unital $F$-algebra, with algebra homomorphisms understood as in [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient], which is finite-dimensional as an $F$-vector space [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace]. Define $F[\epsilon]=F\oplus F\epsilon$ to be the $F$-algebra with componentwise addition, unit $1+0\epsilon$, and multiplication $(a+b\epsilon)(c+d\epsilon)=ac+(ad+bc)\epsilon$; in particular $\epsilon^2=0$. Then either there are an integer $n\geq0$ and an $F$-algebra isomorphism $A\simeq F^n$ with componentwise operations, or there is a surjective unital $F$-algebra homomorphism $A\twoheadrightarrow F[\epsilon]$. The zero algebra is allowed, and $F^0$ denotes the zero algebra.

source.place: Theorem 12.18, proof (b) => (c), printed p.237: the finite-dimensional commutative algebra is a product of local Artinian algebras with residue field F; if one local factor is not a field there is a surjection to the dual numbers. This is the finite-algebra input cited there as CA 16.7, with the zero-algebra case included.

proof.text: If $A$ is the zero algebra, take $n=0$: its unique map to the empty product $F^0$ is an $F$-algebra isomorphism. Henceforth suppose $A\ne0$.

source.place: Theorem 12.18, proof (b) => (c), printed p.237; expansion of the finite-local-algebra argument

proof.text: The field $F$ is a local ring whose only prime ideal is $(0)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-zero-dim-local-discrete-spectrum] to the finite $F$-algebra $A$: it has finitely many maximal ideals $\mathfrak n_1,\ldots,\mathfrak n_r$, and every element of their intersection is nilpotent. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-product-of-localizations-at-maximal] gives the canonical $F$-algebra isomorphism $\alpha:A\xrightarrow{\sim}\prod_{i=1}^r B_i$, where $B_i=A_{\mathfrak n_i}$ is local. If $r=0$, this is the first alternative with $n=0$. For each existing factor, the composite $p_i:A\xrightarrow{\alpha}\prod_jB_j\to B_i$ is surjective: for $b\in B_i$ take $\alpha^{-1}$ of the tuple with entry $b$ at $i$ and zero elsewhere. The images under $p_i$ of a finite $F$-spanning family of $A$ span $B_i$, so each $B_i$ is finite-dimensional over $F$.

source.place: Tag 06RS, lemma-local-dimension-zero-henselian, proof; Tag 00JA, lemma-product-local. These give the product decomposition used by Milne 12.18, p.237.

proof.text: For each $i$, write $\mathfrak m_i$ for the maximal ideal of $B_i$, $s_i:F\to B_i$ for its structure map, and $q_i:B_i\to B_i/\mathfrak m_i$ for the quotient. The quotient is a field, and the images of a finite spanning family of $B_i$ span it over $F$. By [lem-weil-pbc-alg-closed-finite-extension-trivial], $q_is_i:F\to B_i/\mathfrak m_i$ is bijective. Consequently $\rho_i=(q_is_i)^{-1}q_i:B_i\to F$ is an $F$-algebra map with kernel $\mathfrak m_i$ and $\rho_is_i=\operatorname{id}_F$. If every $\mathfrak m_i=0$, every $q_i$ is also bijective; the inverses $s_i^{-1}=\rho_i$ identify $\alpha$ with an $F$-algebra isomorphism $A\simeq F^r$. This proves the first alternative in this case.

source.place: Tag 09GR, lemma-algebraically-closed; applied to the finite residue fields in Milne 12.18, printed p.237.

proof.text: Otherwise select a factor $B=B_i$ with nonzero maximal ideal $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak m_i$, and put $s=s_i$, $\rho=\rho_i$. The finite dimension of $B$ gives Artinianity by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-dim-algebra-artinian]. Since $B$ is local, [lem-weil-pbc-artinian-local-noetherian-nilpotent] gives $\mathfrak m^N=0$ for some $N\ge1$. Hence $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2\ne0$: if $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak m^2$, multiplying by $\mathfrak m$ inductively gives $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak m^t$ for every $t\ge1$, contradicting $\mathfrak m\ne0$ at $t=N$. Regard $V=\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$ as an $F$-vector space via $s$.

source.place: Tags 00J6 (lemma-finite-dimensional-algebra), 00J8 (lemma-artinian-radical-nilpotent), and 00KH (lemma-Noetherian-dimension-0); explicit cotangent nonvanishing expansion of Milne 12.18, printed p.237.

proof.text: Choose $0\ne v\in V$. By [lem-weil-pbc-vector-space-dual-separates], there is an $F$-linear $\lambda:V\to F$ with $\lambda(v)\ne0$. Choose $u_0\in\mathfrak m$ representing $v$ and replace it by $u=\lambda(v)^{-1}u_0$. Then $u\in\mathfrak m$ and $\lambda([u])=1$.

source.place: Theorem 12.18, proof (b) => (c), printed p.237; expansion of the finite-local-algebra argument

proof.text: Define $D:B\to F$ by $D(b)=\lambda([b-s(\rho(b))])$, where the argument lies in $\mathfrak m=\ker\rho$. It is $F$-linear and $D(s(a))=0$ for $a\in F$. To check multiplication, write $b=s(a)+x$, $c=s(d)+y$ with $a=\rho(b)$, $d=\rho(c)$, $x,y\in\mathfrak m$. Then $bc=s(ad)+s(a)y+s(d)x+xy$, and $xy\in\mathfrak m^2$, so $D(bc)=aD(c)+dD(b)$. Therefore $\psi(b)=\rho(b)+D(b)\epsilon$ is additive, sends $1$ to $1$, respects $F$, and satisfies $\psi(bc)=\psi(b)\psi(c)$ for the multiplication of $F[\epsilon]$ in the statement. Thus $\psi$ is a unital $F$-algebra homomorphism.

source.place: Theorem 12.18, proof (b) => (c), printed p.237; expansion of the finite-local-algebra argument

proof.text: For $a,d\in F$, the element $s(a)+du\in B$ satisfies $\rho(s(a)+du)=a$ and $D(s(a)+du)=d\lambda([u])=d$. Thus $\psi(s(a)+du)=a+d\epsilon$, proving surjectivity. Since $p_i:A\to B$ is surjective, so is $\psi p_i:A\twoheadrightarrow F[\epsilon]$, which is the second alternative.

source.place: Theorem 12.18, proof (b) => (c), printed p.237; expansion of the finite-local-algebra argument

Source: Milne AG 12.18 (b)=>(c), printed p.237, read via pdftotext. Milne writes C^vee as a product of local Artinian rings with residue field k (CA 16.7), then says a non-field factor gives a surjection to k[eps] without constructing it. The item states this with the zero algebra added. Its only citer, the multiplicative-additive-vanishing-criterion node, uses it in the matching form. proof_origin=agent is right because steps 4-7 supply the construction Milne omits (D5). Steps: (2) 06RS-proof node gives finitely many primes, all maximal, with nil intersection; this is exactly the hypothesis of the 00JA product node, which gives local factors and an iso that is F-linear; surjective projections and finite dimension of the factors are argued directly. (3) The 09GR node applied to B_i/m_i via q_i s_i gives rho_i with kernel m_i and rho_i s_i=id; if every m_i=0 then A is F^r. (4) 00J6 gives Artinian and 00J8/00KH give m^N=0 with N>=1; m=m^2 would force m=m^t for all t, so m/m^2 is nonzero, with no hidden Nakayama. (5) The dual-separates node gives lambda; rescaling gives lambda([u])=1. (6) I recomputed D(bc)=aD(c)+dD(b) using xy in m^2, so psi is a unital F-algebra map. (7) psi(s(a)+s(d)u)=a+d eps, so psi composed with p_i is surjective. All six cited nodes are Mathlib leaves and their statements say what the steps use; no tool_uses. Small cases: 0, F^r, F[t]/t^2, F[t]/t^3, F[x,y]/(x,y)^2, characteristic 2; algebraic closure is needed (a proper finite extension K is neither alternative). DAG grep for dual-number and Artinian dichotomy nodes found no duplicate; no Lean declaration found under lean/WeilConjectures by id or name variants. No changes.
